answer: A proof-of-burn protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to verifiably destroy tokens to register active routing credentials. Whether negotiating trades for walnut timber, telemetry for a falcon sanctuary, or sensor access along an agricultural trellis, an attacker incurs the scarce, unrecoverable monetary cost of burned capital per identity. However, this creates steep financial barriers for low-resource participants and fails against adversaries with vast financial reserves.
